title: Reducedness and generic density under smooth pullback
statement: Let $S$ be a reduced locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $h:T\to S$ be a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $T$ is reduced and locally Noetherian. Every generic point of an irreducible component of $T$ maps to a generic point of an irreducible component of $S$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components]. For every dense open subset $U\subseteq S$, the inverse image $h^{-1}U$ is dense in $T$, and in each irreducible component of $T$. In particular, if $J\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ is a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] with nowhere dense zero set, its extended ideal $J\mathcal O_T$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] also has nowhere dense zero set. Empty schemes and smooth morphisms whose images omit entire components of $S$ are allowed; no surjectivity or separatedness is assumed.

source.place: ILO Expose VIII Lemma 2.2.9, printed p.91, reducedness and maximal-domination inputs; density input to 2.2.7--2.2.8 and lem-trf-local-term-locality proof (1)--(2). Stacks Tags 034E (descent.tex, lemma-reduced-local-smooth), 01UA (morphisms.tex, lemma-fppf-open), and 00HS (algebra.tex, lemma-flat-going-down).

proof.text: By [lem-pc-smooth-flat], $h$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. The affine presentations of [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] are quotients of polynomial rings in finitely many variables, hence are finitely generated algebras; thus $h$ is locally of finite type in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to the locally Noetherian base $S$ to obtain that $T$ is locally Noetherian.

By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], $h$ has geometrically reduced fibres. For a field $K$ and a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ with image $s$, the morphism factors through $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$, and the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ with $T_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}K$, which is reduced because the fibre $T_s$ is geometrically reduced. Together with flatness from step 1 this verifies the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-flat-geometrically-reduced-pullback]. Apply that statement to $h:T\to S$ and the identity $S\to S$: its reduced locally Noetherian base-change scheme is the given $S$, and its conclusion says $S\times_S T$ is reduced. The maps $T\to S\times_S T$ given by $(h,\operatorname{id}_T)$ and the second projection are inverse by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $T$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 034E (lemma-reduced-local-smooth), ascent direction; geometric-fibre input: morphisms.tex Tag 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), varieties.tex Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal).

proof.text: Let $C$ be an irreducible component of $T$, with generic point $\xi$, and put $s=h(\xi)$. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], choose a component $D$ of $S$ containing $s$, and let $\eta$ be its generic point, supplied by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Then $s\in\overline{\{\eta\}}$. Flat generalization lifting [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] gives $\xi\prime$ with $h(\xi\prime)=\eta$ and $\xi\in\overline{\{\xi\prime\}}$. The irreducible closed set $\overline{\{\xi\prime\}}$ contains $C=\overline{\{\xi\}}$, so maximality of $C$ makes it equal to $C$. Uniqueness of its generic point by [lem-sc-scheme-sober] gives $\xi\prime=\xi$. Consequently $h(\xi)=\eta$. Here specialization is explicitly in the direction $\eta\rightsquigarrow s$ and $\xi\prime\rightsquigarrow\xi$.

source.place: Tag 03HV (lemma-generalizations-lift-flat), equivalently algebra.tex Tag 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down); schemes.tex Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober), topology.tex Tag 004W (lemma-irreducible).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], the flat locally finitely presented $h$ of step 1 is open. Given a nonempty open $W\subseteq T$, its image $h(W)$ is nonempty and open in $S$. Density of $U$ gives a point of $h(W)\cap U$, and by the definition of image this point lifts to $W\cap h^{-1}U$. Hence every nonempty open of $T$ meets $h^{-1}U$, proving density. This argument imposes no surjectivity condition on $h$.

source.place: Tag 01UA (lemma-fppf-open); the density argument is written out from the definition.

proof.text: We also need density on each component. Every component $D$ of $S$ has generic point $\eta_D$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. By [lem-sc-locnoeth-components-locally-finite], take an open neighbourhood $N$ of $\eta_D$ meeting only finitely many components. The point $\eta_D$ belongs to no component other than $D$: a closed component containing it contains its closure $D$, so equals $D$ by maximality. Remove from $N$ all the other components it meets. The result is a nonempty open subset $N_0$ of $S$, contained in $D$ because the components cover $S$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. Since $U$ is dense, $N_0\cap U$ is nonempty. An open of $D$ meeting $D=\overline{\{\eta_D\}}$ contains $\eta_D$, so $\eta_D\in U$. Step 3 now puts every component generic point $\xi$ of $T$ in $h^{-1}U$. Its closure is its component $C$, so $C\cap h^{-1}U$ is dense in $C$. The components cover $T$, giving the density in $T$ as well.

source.place: Tags 004V (definition-irreducible-components), 004W (lemma-irreducible), 0052 (lemma-Noetherian), applied locally on S; schemes.tex Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober).

proof.text: Put $Z=V(J)$, with its defining closed immersion into $S$, and $P=T\times_S Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $p:P\to T$ is a closed immersion. Its kernel ideal is exactly $J\mathcal O_T$ by [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-image-zero-locus] identifies its zero set with $p(P)$. To identify this set, take affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $S$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq h^{-1}V$ of $T$, and set $I=J(V)$. The affine description of a closed immersion in [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] gives $Z|_V=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], its pullback over $W$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A A/I)$. This algebra is $B/IB$: the inverse homomorphisms send $b\otimes\bar a$ to $b h^\sharp(a)$ modulo $IB$ and $\bar b$ to $b\otimes1$; the tensor and quotient relations make both well-defined. A prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ contains $IB$ exactly when its contraction to $A$ contains $I$. Applying the cited image-zero-locus statement on these charts therefore gives $V(J\mathcal O_T)=h^{-1}V(J)$.

The closed set $V(J)$ is nowhere dense by hypothesis, so $U=S\setminus V(J)$ is dense open. Step 4 makes $h^{-1}U$ dense in $T$, and step 6 identifies its closed complement with $V(J\mathcal O_T)$. A closed subset with dense complement has empty interior and is nowhere dense, proving the ideal assertion. If $T$ is empty all source conclusions are vacuous; if $S$ is empty then $T$ is empty as well. Every preceding argument is local or concerns points actually in the image; omitted components, nonseparated schemes, and $J=\mathcal O_S$ cause no exception.
